The '''2020–21 Premier League''' was the 29th season of the [[Premier League]], the top English professional league for association football clubs since its establishment in 1992 and the 122nd season of top-flight English football overall. The season was initially scheduled to start on 8 August 2020 and end on 16 May 2021,<ref name="Sky1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/11927589/premier-league-202021-start-date-confirmed|title=Premier League 2020/21: Season start date confirmed|website=Sky Sports|date=11 September 2020|access-date=21 February 2021}}</ref> but this was delayed until 12 September as a consequence of the [[2019–20 Premier League#Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic|postponement of the previous season's conclusion]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in England|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53530479|title=Premier League: 2020-21 season to start on 12 September|website=BBC Sport|date=24 July 2020|access-date=24 July 2020}}</ref> [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] were the defending champions, having won their first Premier League and nineteenth English league title the previous season. 

In a season largely played behind closed doors, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] secured a fifth Premier League title and seventh English league title overall with three matches to spare; it was also the club's third title in the last four seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2122330|title=Man City claim 2020/21 Premier League title|publisher=Premier League|date=11 May 2021|access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref>

== Summary ==
=== Impact of COVID-19 pandemic ===
At the start of this season, as was the case at the end of the previous season, there was [[Behind closed doors (sport)|limited or no attendance]] at matches besides each team's staff and personnel.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.sky.com/story/premier-league-dates-for-2020-21-season-announced-but-still-no-fans-for-now-12035702|title=Premier League: Dates for 2020-21 season announced - but still no fans for now|publisher=Sky News|date=24 July 2020|access-date=13 August 2020}}</ref> On 23 November 2020, it was announced that some fans would be allowed to return to stadiums in [[The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Restrictions) (All Tiers) (England) Regulations 2020|low-risk areas]] at the end of the second national lockdown on 2 December 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fans at sporting events: Maximum of 4,000 to be allowed in England|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/55010011|date=23 November 2020|access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref> The announcement of a third national lockdown on 4 January 2021, though, signalled a return to matches being played behind closed doors.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/prime-minister-announces-national-lockdown |title=Prime Minister announces national lockdown |date=4 January 2021 |access-date=2 February 2021 |website=gov.uk}}</ref> 

As fans initially were not allowed to attend matches, an agreement was made for all matches to be televised up until at least the October international break. The league's major broadcast partners [[Sky Sports]] and [[TNT Sports (United Kingdom)|BT Sport]] broadcast the vast majority of the matches between them, whilst [[Amazon Prime Video]] and the [[BBC]] were also allotted additional live matches during the season. Following the October international break, Sky and BT trialled a revised format with the launch of a [[pay-per-view]] service for matches not selected for live broadcast on their main channels.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/premier-league-pay-per-view-plan-will-see-fans-have-to-pay-15-to-watch-some-games-in-october-12100282 |title=Premier League pay-per-view plan will see fans have to pay £15 to watch some games in October |date=9 October 2020 |access-date=9 October 2020 |website=Sky News}}</ref> Following strong opposition from fans, the format was discontinued after the November round of international matches and all matches were again shown across the league's four broadcast partners.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/premier-leagues-controversial-pay-per-view-model-to-be-scrapped-12124991 |title=Premier League's controversial pay-per-view model to be scrapped |date=6 November 2020 |access-date=6 November 2020 |website=Sky News}}</ref> This continued for the remainder of the season, making this the first Premier League season in which all matches across the entire campaign were televised.

On 22 February 2021, Prime Minister [[Boris Johnson]] announced as the third step of recovery from the lockdown imposed on 4 January, that subject to certain criteria being met on vaccines, infection rates and new coronavirus variants, large football stadiums would be allowed to reopen on 17 May with a maximum of 10,000 spectators or 25% capacity, whichever was higher.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-56158405|title=Lockdown: Boris Johnson unveils plan to end England restrictions by 21 June|date=22 February 2021|access-date=22 February 2021|work=BBC News}}</ref> This meant that the final round of fixtures scheduled for 23 May would see spectators return to the stadium. To ensure all clubs played their final home game in front of fans, the penultimate round of fixtures were rearranged to take place on 18–19 May. No away fans were permitted for these matches.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Buckingham|first=Philip|title=Each Premier League side will play a match in front of fans before end of season|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4217341/2021/04/15/each-premier-league-side-will-play-a-match-in-front-of-fans-before-end-of-season/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=The Athletic|date=16 April 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Season summary ===
The 2020–21 season began on Saturday 12 September, just seven weeks after the conclusion of the [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20 season]].<ref name="bbc._Prem">{{Cite web |title=Premier League season set for kick-off |author= |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=11 September 2020 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54012403}}</ref> [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] were the defending champions, having won their nineteenth league title the previous season and their first in the Premier League era.<ref name="Sky1"/> As originally planned, the 2020–21 season was to be the second Premier League season with a mid-season break in February, whereby five games of a normal round of ten would be played on one weekend and the remaining five the following weekend.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelner |first1=Martha |title=Premier League winter break to come into force in 2019–20 season |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/08/winter-break-to-come-into-force-in-premier-league-england |access-date=7 April 2019 |work=The Guardian |date=8 June 2018 }}</ref> However, due to the late start of the league and fixture congestion, the winter break was scrapped and instead the 18th round of matches in mid-January was split across two midweeks.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53767120| title= Premier League scraps winter break because of congested 2020-21 schedule| work=[[BBC Sport]]| date=13 August 2020| access-date=13 August 2020}}</ref> It was also the second Premier League season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] (Video Assistant Referee).<ref>{{cite news |title=VAR: Video assistant referees set to be used in Premier League next season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46224473 |access-date=7 April 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 November 2018}}</ref>

==== The race for first place ====
The top of the table was tight for the first months of the season, with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], Liverpool, [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur]] all having occupied first position by late November.<ref name="euro_Prem">{{Cite web |title=Premier League: Jose Mourinho's Tottenham Hotspur go top with impressive win over Manchester City |last=Badshah |first=Nadeem |work=Eurosport UK |date=21 November 2020 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/premier-league/2020-2021/tottenham-hotspur-v-manchester-city-live-premier-league-updates_sto8000463/story.shtml}}</ref> 

==== Liverpool's title defence collapses and Manchester City become Champions ====
Liverpool, despite having suffered a 7-2 loss against [[Aston Villa]] in October, overtook Tottenham again in mid-December, following a meeting between the two clubs at [[Anfield]] which resulted in a {{nowrap|2–1}} win to Liverpool and by Christmas, had opened up a five-point gap following a {{nowrap|7–0}} away win against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref name="bbc._Live">{{Cite web |title=Liverpool beat Spurs to go clear at top |last=McNulty |first=Phil |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 December 2020|access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55241015}}</ref><ref name="bbc._Stun">{{Cite web |title=Stunning Liverpool hit seven past Palace |last=Rindl |first=Josef |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 December 2020 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55268080}}</ref> However, in the new year, they suffered from a significant slump in form. They suffered their first home defeat in 69 games with a {{nowrap|1–0}} defeat to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]],<ref name="bbc._Live_2">{{Cite web |title=Liverpool's unbeaten home run ended by Burnley |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |work=BBC Sport |date=21 January 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55657090}}</ref> which began a run of six consecutive losses at Anfield, following losses to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], Everton, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], dropping to eighth place by early March.<ref name="bbc._Fulh">{{Cite web |title=Fulham win as Liverpool lose sixth straight home game |last=Johnston |first=Neil |work=BBC Sport |date=7 March 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56227460 |quote=Brighton, Manchester City, Everton, Chelsea and now Fulham. }}</ref> [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who were 15th at the beginning of November but sat behind them on goal difference at the start of January, overtook them at the top of the table later that month with a {{nowrap|1–0}} away win against Burnley,<ref name="manu_Matc">{{Cite web |title=Match report: Burnley 0 Man Utd 1 |last=Ganley |first=Joe |publisher=[[Manchester United F.C.]] |date=12 January 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-burnley-v-man-utd-12-january-2021}}</ref> but they were in turn replaced by Manchester City at the end of the month as a {{nowrap|5–0}} Manchester City win over [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] was followed by a {{nowrap|2–1}} home defeat for Manchester United against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref name="bbc._ManC">{{Cite web |title=Man City hammer West Brom to go top |last=Rostance |first=Tom |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55714078}}</ref><ref name="manu_Matc_2">{{Cite web |title=Match report: United 1 Sheffield Utd 2 |last=Mathieson |first=Stuart |work=manutd.com |date=27 January 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-united-v-sheffield-utd-27-january-2021}}</ref> This was to prove the final change of team at the top, as Manchester City, who were 13th in November, went on a 15-match winning streak which saw them 15 points clear of second-place Manchester United after a {{nowrap|4–1}} win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 2 March.<ref name="bbc._'Rem">{{Cite web |title='Remarkable Man City came through hell' |last=Stone |first=Simon |work=BBC Sport |date=2 March 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56164087}}</ref> They went on to secure the title on 12 May 2021 with three matches to spare, following a home defeat for Manchester United against Leicester. It was the club's fifth Premier League title and seventh English league title overall, as well as their third title in the past four seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2122330|title=Man City claim 2020/21 Premier League title|publisher=Premier League|date=11 May 2021|access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref>

==== UEFA Champions League qualification and Chelsea win Champions League ====
Despite missing out on the title, Manchester United finished 2nd whilst managing to go the season unbeaten away from home as they qualified for a second successive season, becoming only the second team in the Premier League era to do so after Arsenal in both [[2001-02 FA Premier League|2001-02]] and their invincible season of [[2003-04 FA Premier League|2003-04]].
The remaining two slots for Champions League qualification were taken by Liverpool and Chelsea. Although Liverpool were 8th with ten games remaining, a run of eight wins from their final ten games, including a 95th-minute winner scored by goalkeeper [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]] against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], saw them recover their position to finish 3rd and qualify for a fifth straight season.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Mane double helps Liverpool beat Palace and finish third|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57132111|access-date=2021-05-25}}</ref> Chelsea endured a difficult start to the season under [[Frank Lampard]], who was sacked in January with the club in 9th position and replaced by [[Thomas Tuchel]]. The club's form improved under Tuchel to secure a second consecutive finish in 4th place, despite a final day defeat to Aston Villa.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea secure top-four finish despite loss at Villa|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57132104|access-date=2021-05-25}}</ref> They won in that season's Champions League final the next week, in the competition's third all-English final against champions Manchester City.

==== UEFA Europa League qualification ====
Leicester enjoyed a successful season, spending more time in the top four places than any other club as well as winning that season's FA Cup against Chelsea; however, three defeats in their final four games, including a home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur on the final day, saw them narrowly finish in 5th for a second consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Leicester miss out on CL after late collapse|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57132108|access-date=2021-05-25}}</ref> Having narrowly avoiding relegation the previous season, [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] surprised many by finishing 6th, their highest finish since [[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/are-west-ham-the-team-of-the-season/191966|title = David Moyes and West Ham: The Premier League's Manager of the Season and Team of the Season duo?}}</ref> Both these clubs earned qualification to the Europa League for the following season.

==== UEFA Europa Conference League qualification ====
Despite leading the table in November, Tottenham suffered a string of poor results from that point onwards. Manager [[José Mourinho|Jose Mourinho]] was sacked in April with the club in 7th place, with [[Ryan Mason]] taking over as interim manager for the rest of the season. Mason was unable to improve the club's position and they finished 7th, their lowest finish since the [[2008–09 Premier League|2008–09 season]], but still good enough to qualify for the brand new third tier Europa Conference League competition.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Meanwhile, their traditional North London rivals Arsenal endured an even worse campaign; despite leading the table in September, eight defeats in their first 14 games left them in 15th just before Christmas and seemingly in danger of being sucked into a relegation battle. Whilst they would pick up enough points thereafter to pull away from the bottom half of the table, the Gunners could only finish 8th for a second successive season as they failed to qualify for European competition for the first time since the [[1994–95 FA Premier League|1994–95 season]].

==== Relegation and Leeds United success ====
On 17 April 2021, [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] were confirmed to be the first team to be relegated to the [[2021–22 EFL Championship|Championship]] following a {{nowrap|1–0}} defeat away to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] with six games remaining, ending their two-year top flight tenure.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 1–0 Sheffield United |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56699182 |access-date=17 April 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 April 2021}}</ref> On 9 May 2021, [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] became the second team to be relegated following a {{nowrap|3–1}} defeat away to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], with three games remaining, immediately returning to the Championship after a season's presence in the top flight.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal 3–1 West Bromwich Albion |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56960423 |access-date=9 May 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2021}}</ref> On 10 May 2021, [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] were the third and final team to be relegated following a 2–0 defeat at home against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] with three games remaining, also immediately returning to the Championship after a season's presence in the top flight. This also marked the first time in the Premier League era that all three teams have been relegated with more than two games to spare and that all three teams didn't reach the 30 point mark in the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fulham 0–2 Burnley |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56967616 |access-date=10 May 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 May 2021}}</ref> In contrast, the final promoted team, [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], finished in 9th with 59 points, the highest points tally for a newly promoted side since [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] (66 points) in [[2000–01 FA Premier League|2000–01]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

== Teams ==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2019–20 EFL Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], after respective top flight absences of sixteen, two and one year(s). They replaced [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] (both teams relegated to the [[2020–21 EFL Championship|Championship]] after five years in the top flight), and [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] (relegated after a year back in the top flight).
